jobs.occupation: Analyst in Capital Planning – Help Shape the Bank’s Financial Future
jobs.description:
Capital planning sits at the heart of how Danske Bank balances financial resilience with sustainable growth. As part of a close-knit analytical team, you will contribute to decisions that enable the bank to serve its customers and support its strategic ambitions. This is a role where your work genuinely matters and where you will build a solid foundation in capital management.

What you will be doing

The Capital Planning team is part of Financial Resource Management in Group Treasury, sitting within Danske Bank's CFO area. The team of seven works on capital target setting, capital issuances, dividend decisions and macroeconomic stress testing. Your analyses and reports will receive close attention from the Executive Leadership Team, the Board of Directors and financial regulators. The atmosphere is collaborative, with knowledge sharing and learning woven into everyday working life, and the team takes pride in delivering high-quality work while enjoying the process.

More specifically, you will:

• Support monthly capital and MREL assessments and projections

• Analyse the effects of regulatory and model changes with relevant teams

• Contribute to stress tests and assessments of capital targets and buffers

• Help analyse payout capacity and capital and MREL funding needs

• Prepare decision material and gradually take ownership of defined deliverables

About you

• Master's degree in economics, finance, business administration or a related field

• Strong analytical skills and a structured, detail-oriented approach

• Ability to communicate complex findings clearly in English

• Curious and collaborative, with an interest in learning and developing within the field

• Comfortable working independently on defined tasks while contributing to team goals

Experience in banking or capital management, and familiarity with Python, SQL or similar tools, would be a welcome addition. We consider candidates at different stages of their career, so we encourage you to apply whether you are just starting out or bring a few years of relevant experience.

What we offer you

You will join a dedicated team where collaboration and continuous learning are part of daily work. We work in a hybrid model, with three to four days per week in the office to support knowledge sharing and team cohesion. You will have room to develop your analytical skills, deepen your understanding of capital management, and take on increasing responsibility over time.

Are you ready for the next step?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, we would be glad to hear from you. Feel free to reach out to hiring manager Henrik Bang at hban@danskebank.dk if you have any questions about the role before applying.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 22 November 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

About the Team

At the Enterprise Process Management (EPM) unit, our north star is “Partnering towards process excellence.” As Danske Bank’s internal consultancy, the Process Intelligence team collaborates across the organization to drive impactful process improvements and embed operational excellence, deliivering real value. We work side-by-side with business units and agile tribes, supporting strategic growth initiatives and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

Our Process Partners play a key role in driving transformations for efficiency and building capabilities in process management. By leveraging Lean methodologies and best practices, we help optimize processes, reduce waste, enhance customer satisfaction and regulatory compliance, and strengthen the organization’s ability to deliver sustainable results. We coach leaders to translate operational excellence principles into lasting behavioural change

What You Will Do

• Drive end-to-end process optimization initiatives, applying Lean principles and eliminating waste.

• Lead and participate in projects focused on customer journeys, process transformation, and change management, using methods such as DMAIC.

• Identify and prioritize organizational benefits, aligning process improvements with business goals and customer needs.

• Acquire and analyze data to uncover improvement opportunities, utilizing Lean and Six Sigma tools and statistical concepts.

• Develop and operationalize process improvement frameworks, ensuring the sustainability and control of implemented solutions.

• Deliver training and mentor colleagues on Lean and process improvement methods, fostering leadership development (both self and others) and a culture of continuous improvement.

• Champion operational excellence by designing and implementing best practices that enhance process performance, ensure compliance, and support the organization’s strategic objectives.

• Coach leaders to embed operational excellence into daily management practices, driving sustainable behavioral change and a culture of continuous improvement.

What We’re Looking For

• Green/Black Belt certification in Lean & Six Sigma, certified Lean Manager or equivalent

• 3+ years of experience in process re-engineering, operational excellence, optimization, or transformation, with strong data analysis skills.

• Project/program management experience (e.g., Agile, Prince2, PMP), with process management or operational excellence as a core methodology.

• Strong skills in business process improvement, change management, and stakeholder engagement.

• Ability to influence without formal authority and thrive in a large, complex organization.

• Experience in delivering training or mentoring on Lean/process improvement.

• Systemic thinking, pragmatic problem-solving, and the ability to structure ambiguity.

• Proven track record in driving and anchoring sustainable change.

• Demonstrated experience in operational excellence, coaching leaders with a proven ability to drive sustainable improvements in efficiency, quality, and business outcomes.

• As an advantage: knowledge in AI application for process and operational excellence work.

• Advanced English language skills

Want to Know More?

If you have any questions, you are welcome to reach out to Laura Makele, Head of Process Intelligence on lmak@danskebank.lt or Indre Sliziene, Head of Operational Excellence on isli@danskebank.lt

Diversity & Inclusion

Together, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates diversity.

jobs.occupation: Finance Business Partner – Large Corporates & Institutions
jobs.description:
Danske Bank is the preferred bank for large corporate and institutional customers across the Nordics, and this role sits at the heart of the financial steering that helps LC&I deliver on that promise. As Finance Business Partner for the Markets IT Development area, you will translate financial insight into decisions that shape how three Tribes operate and invest. In return, you will grow your career within a collaborative team that values openness and genuine flexibility.

What you will be doing

You will join a dedicated team of Finance Business Partners anchored in LC&I Performance Management within the CFO Area. The team works closely with senior management across Markets IT Development, Payments, and Asset Management, sharing analysis that feeds directly into financial steering decisions. The atmosphere is informal and collaborative, with a shared belief that clear financial insight creates real value for the business.

In your day-to-day work, you will:

• Act as Finance Business Partner for the Markets IT Development area, covering three Tribes

• Represent the CFO Area in the area's management team meetings

• Coordinate monthly and annual financial planning and analysis processes

• Assess financial implications of prioritisation decisions and track expected benefits

• Support a more data-driven approach to decision-making across the area

About you

• Relevant master's-level degree in finance, economics, or a related field

• Experience in FP&A, performance management, or business partnering is beneficial but not required

• Ability to build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders through clear communication

• Interest in data analytics and digitisation; strong Excel skills are an advantage

• Comfortable navigating a large, complex organisation with multiple priorities

• Proficient in written and spoken English

If you have experience working alongside IT development teams or within a financial institution, that would be a welcome addition to the team.

What we offer you

This role offers you the chance to develop your finance career within one of the leading Nordic banks, working alongside colleagues who are genuinely committed to collaboration and knowledge sharing. We work in a hybrid model with three to four days per week in the office, balancing flexibility with a strong team culture. You will have access to learning opportunities and a working environment that encourages new approaches and personal growth.

Are you ready for the next step?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, we encourage you to apply. Feel free to reach out to hiring manager, Muhammad Zohaib, at zoh@danskebank.dk or Strategic Investment Partner, Daniel Bahne Kvesel, at dakv@danskebank.dk if you have any questions about the role before applying.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 22 November 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Operational information is the backbone of how a bank operates, and getting it right matters.

We are looking for an experienced and strategic leader to strengthen the Group-wide operational information blueprint, with accountability anchored in the Operational Design & Governance team within Enterprise Process Management.

In this role, you will lead a critical Group-wide capability, strengthening how we design, structure and govern operational information across the Group. You will strengthen the foundations for simpler and more transparent operations, effective transformation, regulatory readiness, automation and AI adoption.

Your role

Your mission is to mature and strengthen the Group-wide operational information model, making it increasingly coherent, consistent, scalable and fit for both commercial and regulatory needs, while driving its adoption across the organisation.

You will lead a team of 16 specialists within Enterprise Process Management and own the direction and evolution of the Group’s operational information capability. Working across organisational boundaries, you will collaborate closely with Business Units, Enterprise Architecture, Risk, Compliance, Technology and Transformation teams.

More specifically, you will:

• 
Lead and develop a high-performing team of specialists while building a collaborative and outcome-focused culture.

• 
Set clear direction for the Group operational information model design and establish clear methodologies, standards and governance across the Group.

• 
Strengthen operational governance and accountability across functions, value chains, business services, processes, manual services, SOPs and business procedures.

• 
Drive adoption and execution, ensuring frameworks and standards translate into practical and scalable solutions across the Bank.

• 
Create foundations for AI, automation and data-driven operations through high-quality operational information and strong design principles.

• 
Partner across the Bank, connecting business, operations, architecture, technology, data, risk, controls and transformation perspectives.

• 
Advise and guide senior stakeholders on operational information design, governance and operating model decisions.

What we are looking for

You are an experienced and strategic leader who combines enterprise thinking with the ability to turn direction into execution.

You bring:

• 
Proven leadership experience from leading large specialist or transformation teams with a broad range of deliverables.

• 
Strong expertise in business architecture, process management and/or operating model design.

• 
Strong business acumen and the ability to connect strategic objectives with operational realities.

• 
A strategic mindset combined with strong execution capabilities and a track record of delivering measurable outcomes.

• 
Experience driving enterprise-wide change in a complex and regulated environment, preferably financial services.

• 
Strong ability to navigate complexity, influence senior stakeholders and drive alignment across organisational boundaries.

• 
Experience establishing and implementing methodologies, standards, frameworks and governance models.

• 
A strong understanding of how business, operations, technology, data, risk and controls connect across the enterprise.

• 
An interest in how operational information design and governance can create the foundations for AI, automation and analytics.

• 
Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, combined with a passion for developing people and teams.

What success looks like

You will help create an operating environment where operational information is well-designed, governed and trusted; complexity is reduced; accountability is clear; and the Bank is better equipped to execute transformation and adopt new technologies at scale.

Success will ultimately mean making it easier for the organisation to understand how we operate, how our operations connect, and where we need to change.

Why join us?

You will lead a critical EPM capability at the intersection of business design, governance, transformation, technology, data and AI. The role offers significant scope to influence how the Bank operates at scale and to help build a simpler, more coherent and future-ready organisation.

You will work with a broad network of senior stakeholders across the Bank and have the opportunity to develop an area that will become increasingly important as we accelerate transformation, automation and AI adoption.

We work in a hybrid model, with 3 to 4 days per week in the office to support collaboration and knowledge sharing. You will have access to learning resources, a broad network of senior stakeholders, and genuine opportunities to grow as a leader.

Are you ready for the next step?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, please reach out to hiring manager Inga Rimké-Linga at inri@danskebank.dk with any questions, or apply directly.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 17 November 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Danske Bank

Inga Rimké-Linga inri@danskebank.dk

At Saxo, we believe that security enables our business to grow, innovate, and serve clients with confidence. We are looking for a highly experienced Head of Physical Security & Safety to lead and strengthen our global physical security framework, ensuring the protection of our employees, facilities, assets, and operations across all Saxo locations.

This is a unique opportunity to shape and mature a critical capability within a global financial institution while influencing security standards, processes, and culture across multiple locations.

About the role

As Head of Physical Security & Safety, you will be responsible for protecting Saxo's people, facilities, operations and reputation across multiple international locations.

You will lead the development of our physical security framework, drive risk-based security initiatives, strengthen preparedness and crisis response capabilities, and ensure that security remains aligned with the evolving threat landscape.

You will work closely with senior stakeholders, facility management, IT Security, Risk, Compliance, and international office representatives to ensure a consistent and robust security posture across the bank.

Your responsibilities

• 
Lead Saxo's physical security and safety programme across global locations.

• 
Identify, assess and mitigate threats and vulnerabilities affecting employees, facilities and business operations.

• 
Develop and implement security policies, standards and operating procedures.

• 
Drive incident management, investigations and corrective actions where required.

• 
Strengthen emergency preparedness, crisis response and resilience capabilities.

• 
Oversee physical security technologies including access control, CCTV and alarm systems.

• 
Provide strategic security advice to senior management and key stakeholders.

• 
Manage security service providers and external security partners.

• 
Promote a security-aware culture through training and awareness programmes.

• 
Support major events, critical incidents and business continuity initiatives.

Your profile

You may come from law enforcement, the military, intelligence services, critical infrastructure, corporate security or a similar environment where security, risk management and operational leadership have been central to your role.

We expect you to bring:

• Extensive experience within physical security, protective security or security operations.

• A strong understanding of threat assessment, risk management and incident response.

• Experience leading security programmes, projects or specialist teams.

• The ability to advise and influence senior stakeholders.

• A calm and structured approach in high-pressure situations.

• Strong personal integrity, sound judgement and discretion.

• Fluency in English and Danish.

We get curious people invested in the world

When you work at Saxo, you become a Saxonian and part of a purpose-driven organisation, where good ideas are always taken seriously, and where you can make a true impact. We are invested in your development, and you can expect a robust career from day one when you join Saxo – no matter which role you take on.

You will join 2,500 other ambitious colleagues across 11 countries and become part of an international organisation. Working in Saxo, you will get to meet colleagues from many different cultures and backgrounds, and you should know that we value diversity and inclusion and see it as a genuine source of strength to drive growth, foster innovation and position us for long-term success.

We encourage an open feedback culture and supportive team environments enabling employees to grow and fulfil their career aspirations.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Product Manager for the DK Pension to take responsibility for the ongoing management and development of Saxo’s Danish pension offering.

About the job

The role combines pension domain responsibility with senior product management. You will work with the regulatory, operational and commercial aspects of the pension offering, while also helping to drive the product roadmap and digital development.

You will collaborate across business, technology and control functions and play an important role in translating pension regulation, client needs and business requirements into product priorities and solutions.

Key responsibilities

DK Pension and domain management

• Take responsibility for the Danish pension offering and its ongoing development

• Maintain a strong understanding of Danish bank pension regulation, taxation and relevant market developments, and translate changes into business and product requirements

• Help ensure that the pension offering remains compliant and operationally sound in collaboration with Legal, Compliance, Tax and Operations

• Act as a pension subject-matter expert and point of contact across relevant parts of the organisation

• Support operational teams with pension-related processes, requirements and work instructions where needed

• Manage relationships with an external pension vendor as well as partners, including new requirements, changes and prioritisation

• Participate in external forums and working groups to keep current with market best practices and upcoming regulatory changes

Senior Product Management

• Own and develop the product vision and roadmap for the pension offering, balancing regulatory requirements, client needs and business priorities

• Work with the Head of Pension to manage and prioritise the development backlog based on business needs, client value, regulatory requirements and technical dependencies

• Translate pension, tax and regulatory requirements into clear product and development requirements

• Work closely with technology teams throughout development and implementation

• Coordinate across Technology, Onboarding, Operations, Legal, Compliance and other relevant stakeholders

• Contribute to the continued development of the digital pension customer journey, including opportunities to improve usability and self-service

• Follow initiatives from initial requirements through implementation and subsequent improvements

Your profile

We are looking for someone with practical knowledge of pensions and experience from the Danish financial sector who is comfortable working with both product development and regulatory requirements.

You may currently work within a pension company, bank, investment firm or another regulated financial institution.

We expect that you bring:

• Relevant professional experience from the Danish financial sector, with experience related to bank pension framework; ratepension, aldersopsparing and kapitalpension

• Good knowledge of Danish pension products and the regulatory and tax framework surrounding them

• Experience from a product-focused role, such as Product Owner, Product Manager, pension product specialist, business developer or a similar position

• Experience translating regulatory, business or operational requirements into product solutions

• Experience working with digital development and prioritising requirements or a product backlog

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills

• A structured approach to prioritisation and the ability to work with regulatory, operational, commercial and client considerations simultaneously

• Fluent in Danish and English

Nice to have

• Experience with digital investment or trading platforms

• Knowledge of Aktiesparekonto (ASK) and the broader Danish investment and savings landscape

• Experience collaborating with external pension providers, administrators or technology vendors

• A member of external forums and established working groups with deep technical expertise & an industry-wide network

About you

You have a solid understanding of pensions and an interest in how pension products can be developed and improved through digital solutions.

You are comfortable working with different types of stakeholders, from Compliance and Legal to Operations and Technology, and can translate pension-related requirements into practical solutions.

The role could suit someone who has already worked as a Product Owner or Product Manager within pensions, but it could also be relevant for an experienced pension professional who has worked closely with digital product development.

You combine pension knowledge with a structured and collaborative approach and are comfortable taking responsibility for both the day-to-day product agenda and the longer-term development of the pension offering.

About the Role

As a Tax Services Product Specialist, you will help shape and develop Saxo’s global tax service offering, connecting tax expertise with investment products, custody infrastructure and technology.

You will design, improve and evolve processes across withholding tax, Relief at Source, tax reclaims, documentation, beneficial owner disclosure and financial transaction taxes, turning complex tax and market requirements into practical, scalable solutions.

Working across Tax Operations, Corporate Actions, Custody, Product, Technology, Compliance and Legal, you will translate regulatory and market developments into effective tax services, processes and controls. You will also collaborate with custodians, paying agents and tax service providers internationally.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys solving complex problems, connecting the dots across functions and turning specialist tax knowledge into better products and services.

Key areas of responsibility include:

• Define and maintain tax services, tax treatment rules, investor classifications and operational requirements, including eligibility, limitations and controls.

• Work with Operations, Product and Technology to enhance tax processes, system solutions and automation, and implement new tax and custody solutions.

• Support tax remittance processes covering withholding taxes, financial transaction taxes, stamp duties and other local tax requirements.

• Investigate tax-related incidents and client cases, identify root causes and drive remediation, process improvements and service documentation.

• Work with custodians, paying agents, tax vendors and other providers, while providing tax subject-matter expertise and supporting risk assessments, controls, audits and regulatory reviews.

Your profile

The role is suited to professionals with experience in investment tax, custody, securities services, corporate actions, asset servicing or related areas within financial services.

Relevant experience and knowledge may include:

• Experience in tax operations, custody, securities services, corporate actions or asset servicing.

• Knowledge of withholding tax and cross-border investment taxation.

• Experience with tax processes, documentation, Relief at Source, tax reclaims or beneficial owner disclosure.

• Ability to interpret tax guidance, regulatory requirements and market practices.

• Experience translating requirements into processes, controls or system solutions.

• Experience working with global custodians, intermediaries or service providers.

• Strong analytical skills and experience resolving tax or operational cases.

• Experience developing procedures, service documentation or control frameworks.

• Ability to communicate complex tax and operational topics to different stakeholders.

• Experience collaborating effectively across functions and with external partners.

Additional Relevant Experience

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be beneficial:

• Global custody models, including omnibus and segregated structures.

• Financial transaction taxes, stamp duties and other investment taxes.

• Regulatory or market change initiatives.

• Tax product or service development.

• Tax technology, automation or system implementation.

• Multi-market tax remittance and reporting.

• Service governance, operational risk or controls.

More about the role

The position provides the opportunity to work across international markets, tax regimes and custody networks and contribute to the ongoing development of Saxo’s tax service offering.

The role combines tax subject-matter knowledge with custody, operations, service development and technology. It therefore provides exposure to both the technical requirements associated with investment taxation and the operational and system solutions required to deliver tax services at scale.

_Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for a Global Mobility Manager to join our office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Team

You will join a global People team of more than 15 colleagues with diverse responsibilities and mandates. You will be part of the HR Legal & Mobility team, which comprises six colleagues.

Role

As Global Mobility Manager, you will manage global mobility cases and key operational workstreams across global tax, social security, immigration and relocation.

You will advise internal stakeholders on mobility processes, coordinate complex cross-border matters with specialist advisers, and ensure timely delivery in line with Mobility Policies and approval requirements.

Working closely with People, Payroll, Finance and external providers, you will identify risks early and lead improvements to mobility processes, systems and employee experience.

Responsibilities will include:

• Manage mobility cases end to end across global tax, social security, immigration and relocation, resolving complex issues.

• Oversee mobility compliance, documentation and data controls, including timely and accurate reporting of taxable vendor benefits.

• Advise stakeholders on mobility arrangements and policies, turning global specialist advice into action.

• Manage vendor performance, costs and escalations, including invoice review and internal cost recovery.

• Support stakeholder reporting on mobility progress, costs, risks and recommendations.

• Support mobility process improvements, including workflow optimization, integration and data management, and contribute to policy updates and implementation.

You

You have a relevant university degree and 5+ years of experience in global mobility within an international business or professional services firm.

You have experience managing cross-border mobility cases, coordinating tax, social security and immigration, and leading operational workstreams.

You are comfortable advising business stakeholders, managing external providers and exercising sound judgment on when to resolve matters independently and when to seek specialist input or escalate.

You also have a genuine interest in using AI and technology to improve service delivery and ways of working.

We look for the following in a candidate:

• Solid business acumen and ability to translate specialist advice into practical recommendations.

• Proven ability to own multiple cases and projects, coordinate contributors and resolve issues to deliver agreed outcomes.

• Sound judgment and initiative, with a structured, detail-oriented approach to prioritizing, anticipating dependencies and adapting to changing business needs.

• Experience optimizing mobility processes and implementing them within a mobility system is considered an advantage, but not a requirement.

• Fluency in English, both spoken and written.

The process

Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

CIP Fund Solutions’ commitment to diversity and inclusion

CIP Fund Solutions is committed to securing a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels respected and heard.

A diverse workforce allows CIP Fund Solutions to achieve results through different approaches and solutions to task execution and problem solving. We want all our employees to have equal opportunities for personal growth and career opportunities regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, nationality, or ethnicity.

CIP Fund Solutions

CIP FS’ purpose is to enable CIP’s ambition to scale rapidly over the coming strategy-period - supporting our colleagues with professional and efficient financial, legal, tax and business operations through the cycle from fund formation and capital raising, to deploying investments into construction of large-scale greenfield renewable energy assets, as well as M&A.

For more information, please visit CIP Fund Solutions.

Become part of Group Internal Audit and help improve Danske Bank’s resilience by delivering assurance for the Group’s second line of defense Regulatory Compliance function. You will assess how regulatory compliance risks are identified, monitored, challenged and reported, using risk-based auditing, data analytics and AI-enabled tools to deliver meaningful insight across the organisation.

What you will be doing

You will lead, or contribute to, audits of the Group’s second line of defence Regulatory Compliance function, assessing governance, risk management and controls across regulatory compliance.

In this role, you will:

• Plan and conduct audits covering areas such as compliance risk assessments and Group Wide Risk Assessments, risk-based activity planning, compliance oversight and monitoring, management information and reporting

• Perform audits of specific regulatory compliance risk areas, including market integrity and market abuse surveillance, conflicts of interest, regulatory engagement, conduct risk and emerging compliance risks associated with new technologies and AI

• Apply professional scepticism, data analytics and technology-enabled audit techniques to identify risk patterns, test controls and deliver impactful audit insights

• Engage confidently with stakeholders at all organisational levels, communicate audit conclusions clearly and concisely, and monitor the timely resolution of audit findings and risk mitigation actions

• Contribute to the continuous development of audit methodologies, data-driven auditing techniques and the use of AI-enabled tools within Group Internal Audit

About you

We imagine that you bring:

• Several years of experience in internal audit, compliance, external audit, consulting, risk management or a comparable role in financial services

• Strong understanding of regulatory compliance risks, governance frameworks and the role of a second line Regulatory Compliance function

• Ability to assess complex regulatory and governance topics and communicate clear, well-supported conclusions to senior stakeholders

• Strong communication, stakeholder management and project management skills

• Strong analytical skills and an interest in leveraging data analytics and technology-enabled auditing techniques

We welcome candidates who bring curiosity, professional judgement and a commitment to continuous learning. Familiarity with AI-enabled audit tools or specific regulatory areas such as market abuse surveillance, conduct risk or regulatory engagement would be an advantage, but is not a requirement.

What we offer you

We invest in your development through training that matches your career aspirations. You will work in a collaborative environment that values different perspectives, professional curiosity and innovative thinking.

As part of Group Internal Audit, you will deliver independent assurance, insight and foresight and gain a unique enterprise-wide perspective on Regulatory Compliance’s risks, governance and control practices across the Group.

Our hybrid working model supports 3 to 4 days per week in the office, enabling close collaboration, knowledge sharing and professional development.

Are you ready for the next step?

If you are motivated by understanding how regulatory compliance risks are managed at Group level and want to apply your experience in an independent assurance role, we would be pleased to hear from you. If you have any questions before applying, please reach out to hiring manager, Christoffer Øhauge Pedersen at chrpe@danskebank.dk.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 4 December 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Would you like to help shape the future of SAP at Danish Crown?

At Danish Crown, we are transforming our SAP landscape. We are looking for an experienced SAP Technical Lead who can bring specialists together and turn complex business requirements into robust technical solutions, from architecture and development to go-live and operational handover.

Joining Global IT, you will work across the SAP programme, business units and group functions. In close collaboration with architects, functional leads, technical specialists and external partners, you will connect business needs with technical delivery and ensure that our SAP solutions are scalable, secure and ready for long-term operation.

Your role as SAP Technical Lead

As SAP Technical Lead, you will own the technical direction and quality of SAP solutions across the transformation programme. You will provide technical governance across development, integration, platform services, security and operations, keeping delivery aligned with business requirements, architecture and IT roadmaps. Your leadership will be technical and collaborative, guiding specialists and partners across teams and domains.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• Define and maintain technical principles, standards and solution designs, support architectural roadmaps and review integrations, extensions and non-functional requirements.

• Lead and coordinate technical delivery across SAP Basis, development, SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP), integration, security and external partners, applying agile delivery principles.

• Own technical analysis, estimates, peer reviews, documentation and quality assurance, while identifying and resolving technical risks, dependencies and decisions.

• Support technical and performance testing, cutover and deployment, and ensure that monitoring, support models, documentation and operational handover are ready before go-live.

• Lead complex troubleshooting and root-cause analysis across teams and suppliers to deliver secure, supportable solutions that comply with our standards.

• Advise programme leadership, business stakeholders and senior management, facilitate technical workshops and mentor specialists through knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.

Who are you?

You enjoy turning complex business and programme requirements into practical technical solutions. With a structured, pragmatic approach, you create clarity, make informed decisions and maintain progress when requirements are not yet fully defined. You communicate options and recommendations clearly and build strong working relationships with both technical specialists and business stakeholders.

We imagine that you bring:

• Relevant higher education in IT, computer science, engineering or a comparable discipline.

• Extensive technical leadership experience from complex SAP programmes or transformations.

• Strong experience with SAP S/4HANA and related platforms, development and integration technologies.

• Experience coordinating internal specialists, implementation partners and vendors in a complex, matrix-based and business-critical environment.

• Strong analytical, problem-solving and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to balance competing priorities.

jobs.occupation: PhD fellowship concerning translational tissue engineering for urethral reconstructions
jobs.description:
The Department of Pediatric Surgery at Julianne Marie Center, Rigshospitalet, is offering a three-year PhD fellowship. The PhD fellowship is within the field of pediatric surgery and tissue engineering and is available from December 1, 2026 or as soon as possible thereafter. The Novo Nordisk Tandem Programme finances this PhD fellowship.

Aim of the PhD project

To conduct preclinical in vitro and in vivo studies to develop and evaluate perioperative layered autologous tissue expansion grafts for male urethral reconstruction.

Project description

Highly specialized centres in Paediatric Surgery and Urology treat children with a wide range of congenital malformations affecting the urinary and genital systems. Conditions such as bladder exstrophy, cloacal exstrophy, severe hypospadias, posterior urethral valves, and spina bifida may significantly affect the development and function of the urinary bladder and urethra. In most cases, surgical reconstruction can successfully restore anatomy and function. However, in more complex cases, tissue deficiency, poor tissue quality, and impaired innervation can pose major challenges to surgical reconstruction. These complications may result in substantial morbidity and, in some cases, even threaten the child's life. Long-term consequences can include impaired organ function, recurrent illness, dependence on medication, repeated surgical interventions, and lifelong medical care.

Reconstruction of tubular structures is particularly important in congenital urinary tract malformations. Examples include creating catheterizable channels to facilitate bladder emptying, reconstructing the penile urethra, and replacing or reconstructing the ureter to ensure adequate urine drainage from the kidney to the bladder. The overall aim of this project is to develop novel regenerative medicine approaches for reconstructive surgery in children with severe congenital malformations, with the ultimate goal of reducing morbidity and improving long-term quality of life. Specifically, the PhD project will focus on developing autologous tissue-engineered grafts for urethral reconstruction.

The scientific novelty lies in exploiting the body's own capacity for tissue regeneration by using the body as a bioreactor. This approach, referred to as guided tissue engineering, enables the development of autologous grafts in vivo, without the need for complex ex vivo cell expansion or specialized cell culture facilities. The method has the potential to be simple, cost-effective, and readily transferable to standard surgical settings, thereby making regenerative treatment accessible to a broader patient population. If successful, the approach could pave the way for clinical implementation, initially targeting patients with severe hypospadias who require complex urethral reconstruction.

Beyond paediatric reconstructive surgery, the findings may also have broader applications in other patient populations requiring tissue reconstruction, including adults undergoing reconstructive surgery following cancer treatment or severe trauma.

The PhD programme will comprise both in vitro studies and in vivo animal experiments to investigate and evaluate tissue-engineered constructs incorporating biomaterials and autologous tissues, with particular emphasis on their regenerative potential and suitability for reconstructive surgery.
